title: Reading Study for AI-Segmentation in PET/CT: Ready for Prime Time?
summary: This study investigates whether the reporting of PET/CT examinations by radiologists and nuclear medicine physicians can be accelerated by artificial intelligence (AI) without compromising report quality. For this purpose, a web-based platform is used where readers assess cases with and without AI support. The aim is to determine whether AI can make reporting more efficient and reliable.
conditions: Other and unspecified types of non-Hodgkin lymphoma

interventions.name:
In this study, 60 retrospective clinical PET/CT examinations (PSMA and FDG PET/CT, either initial staging or follow-up) from LMU Klinikum are selected, anonymized, and segmented using AI (LesionTracer) as well as manual reference segmentation.
The readers (radiologists/nuclear medicine physicians)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients: Retrospective cohort of 60 cases with PSMA- or FDG-PET/CT (staging or follow-up) from LMU Klinikum.
- Readers: Board-certified or in training in Radiology/Nuclear Medicine with ≥6 months of PET/CT experience, able to report in German.
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients: PET/CT acquisition not at LMU Klinikum, insufficient image quality.
- Readers: missing informed consent, incomplete readings, non-German reports, obvious misconduct, involvement in the RIPE study team.
